scenes.say: Ever wonder how Kafka guarantees your messages arrive? Let's break down the three delivery semantics you need to know.
At-most-once means some messages might be lost, but you'll never see duplicates. At-least-once guarantees no data loss, but you might get the same message more than once.

scenes.label: Exactly-once
scenes.sub: No loss, no duplicates. Needs transactions.
scenes.say: Exactly-once is the gold standard. No missing data, no repeats. But you need transactions and idempotent producers to pull it off.

rows.b: Low risk if some data is lost
Duplication is okay, loss is not

scenes.say: Pick your delivery semantic based on how critical data loss or duplication is for your business. It's all about trade-offs.

scenes.question: Does at-least-once mean no duplicates?
scenes.right: No, at-least-once can cause duplicates if processing fails after offset commit.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap. At-least-once doesn't mean no duplicates. If processing fails after you commit, you can get repeats.
